head: 24ebf8f5debf85be1fb12c93accb93017ca150d8

findings.issue: fixed: Network text takes precedence over explicit auth/quota/model/config failures; a wall timeout without network evidence is also marked retryable. This loses wait-human/config/cooldown dispositions.
fixed: The quota regex treats the JSON field spendControlReached as exhaustion even when its value is false, masking an unrelated model failure.
fixed: A merely listed model with available login/quota is labeled backend=ready and full backend verified, without execution verification.
fixed: cliPreflightKey is called without its provider argument, so Codex auth.json/config.toml changes do not invalidate the Herdr cache.

fixed: Production preflight caches only server health text; the new observation helpers are unused, so launcher hash, provider, requested/reported model, observation time and source are absent from the cached receipt.

fixed: The surrounding adapter returns raw launcher stdout/stderr as RunResult.output, allowing credentials/cookies into downstream records despite AC5. Preflight also interpolates an unvalidated protocol value. Redact output before truncation and validate protocol before logging.

needs-human: configured requestedModel affects admission/cache only and is never passed to the launcher. The launcher model-selection contract must be established before forwarding a new parameter or rejecting configuration.

needs-human: retry/cooldown advice is only embedded in text; every failed run remains recoveryRequired and scheduler.ts quarantines it before retries/cooldown or normal attempt accounting. A verified-stop/recovery contract is required; do not remove the safety fence.

needs-human: Herdr and underlying CLI versions/hashes and Pi authorization-profile identity are not observed or bound to the cache. Launcher fingerprint alone does not satisfy the exact runtime identity acceptance criterion.

needs-human: allowedFallbacks is used to authorize the configured primary provider, so an empty fallback list blocks the primary. Existing new tests explicitly require this behavior, while the issue describes a fallback allowlist; resolve this policy contract before changing it.

needs-human: the PR includes three issue #13 commits changing regression fixtures and test-skip boundaries, beyond the stated issue #34 readiness scope. Decide whether to retain or separate that history; do not silently revert testing changes during this review.

summary: Fixed six review defects covering failure classification, boolean quota signals, verified readiness, Codex cache invalidation, observation provenance and safe diagnostics, with 18 regression/control cases. Git Bash typecheck, build and all 2,048 tests in 204 files passed. Five needs-human gaps remain for requested-model enforcement, recovery-safe retry/cooldown, runtime/Pi identity, primary-versus-fallback policy and issue #13 scope; the real-backend canary was not run.
